correctness.rationale: Disk supports add. Central symmetry and the squared distances to an antipodal pair of maximal norm force the unique enclosing-ball center to be zero. As an independent route to the global maximizer, write z_i=u_i² and s=sum_A z_i. At fixed s, Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the two edge sums separately by sqrt(binomial(a,2)(a−1)s) and sqrt(ab[bs+a(1−s)]). Both bounds are attained at classwise equal squared coordinates. Equality in the positively weighted cross sum forces all z_i+z_j constant over cross edges, hence all z_i equal within each class, including a=2 or b=1. Maximizing the resulting scalar function yields s=1 for b≥a, or for b<a below and at the stated threshold; the derivative at 1 has sign (a−1)/sqrt(2)−τ(a−b), and strict concavity with positive infinite derivative at 0 gives the unique interior solution beyond the threshold. An attaining support direction gives exactly the contact Ru by equality in Cauchy–Schwarz, and the reverse map is x↦x/R. Thus the contact counts and their antipodal diameter counts exhaust the possibilities. The formal squared branch difference is ab(a−b)(τ−τ_c)², giving the second derivative jump, and the derivative of (1−s)/b at τ_c from above is 2sqrt(2)(a−b)/[a(a−1)], giving the square-root onset.
correctness.replay: Use the two fixed-s support bounds above and the scalar stationarity equation in RESULT.md lines 68–83. A separate symbolic expansion and differentiation reproduced the branch gap and the derivative of (1−s)/b. Substitutions at τ=1 give 34+24sqrt(2) for (a,b)=(4,2) and 350/3 with s=20/21 for (5,2). The packaged verify.py was inspected, not executed; its grid and sampled points are corroboration, not exhaustion.
residual_risks: The proof uses positive cross weight and the standard Euclidean metric. It concerns the minimum enclosing ball, not in general the minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid.

value.rationale: The enclosing ball and its contacts are intrinsic metric quantities of graph-indexed disk sums. With the edge set fixed and every disk radius positive, varying just the cross weight changes which coordinates can appear at a contact, producing exactly a jump from 2^a to 2^(a+b) contacts and a sharp loss of radial smoothness. The quantitative onset and complete equality cases add geometric information beyond solving a single radius example or bounding it by an ellipsoid.
residual_risks: This is a two-class weighted family. It does not classify arbitrary weighted disk sums, algebraic boundaries or minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoids.
